learningObjectives.title: The end of the Cold War and beyond

questions.q: Which wartime conference of February 1945, held before Germany's surrender, was attended by Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin?
questions.explain: Yalta (February 1945) brought the 'Big Three' together to plan the post-war world while the war in Europe continued.

questions.q: Who represented the USA as President at the Potsdam Conference in July 1945?
questions.explain: Roosevelt had died in April 1945, so Truman attended Potsdam as the new US President.

questions.q: What was the main aim of the Truman Doctrine, announced in 1947?
options: To contain the spread of communism
questions.explain: The Truman Doctrine committed the USA to a policy of containment, offering support to nations resisting communism.

questions.q: Why did Stalin view the Marshall Plan of 1947 as a threat to the USSR?
options: He feared it would extend American influence over Europe
He believed it would rearm Germany's military
He thought it broke the terms of the Yalta Conference
He worried it would strengthen the League of Nations
questions.explain: Stalin saw the offer of US economic aid as 'dollar imperialism' designed to draw European countries into the American sphere.

questions.q: The Berlin Airlift of 1948-49 was the Western response to which Soviet action?
options: The building of the Berlin Wall
The testing of the atomic bomb
questions.explain: Stalin blockaded land routes into West Berlin, so the West flew in supplies for almost a year.

questions.q: Which defensive military alliance did Western nations, including the USA and Britain, form in 1949?
questions.explain: The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation was created in 1949 to provide collective Western defence against the Soviet bloc.

questions.q: When Churchill spoke of an 'Iron Curtain' in his 1946 Fulton speech, what was he describing?
options: The growing division of Europe into East and West
The blockade of the port of Berlin
The border between North and South Korea
questions.explain: Churchill used the phrase to warn that Soviet control was sealing off Eastern Europe from the democratic West.

questions.q: Who was the reforming leader of the 1956 Hungarian Uprising, later executed after Soviet intervention?
questions.explain: Imre Nagy led Hungary's attempt at reform in 1956 and was executed after Soviet tanks crushed the uprising.

questions.q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
questions.explain: East Germany began building the Berlin Wall in 1961 to divide the city.

questions.q: Why did East Germany and the USSR build the Berlin Wall in 1961?
options: To stop East Germans fleeing to the West through Berlin
To protect East Berlin from a NATO invasion
To block Western food supplies into the city
To mark the border agreed at the Potsdam Conference
questions.explain: Millions had escaped to the West via Berlin, so the Wall was built to halt this damaging 'brain drain'.

questions.q: In which year did the Cuban Missile Crisis take place?
questions.explain: The Cuban Missile Crisis, the closest the world came to nuclear war, occurred in October 1962.

questions.q: Why was the discovery of Soviet nuclear missiles on Cuba so alarming to the USA?
options: Cuba was close enough for the missiles to strike US cities
Cuba controlled Western access to West Berlin
The missiles broke the terms of the Warsaw Pact
Cuba was a member of NATO
questions.explain: Cuba lay only about 90 miles from Florida, placing many American cities within range of the missiles.

questions.q: After the Cuban Missile Crisis, leaders wanted to reduce the risk of accidental war. Which measure was set up as a direct result?
options: A 'hotline' telephone link between Washington and Moscow
The building of the Berlin Wall
The formation of the Warsaw Pact
questions.explain: A direct 'hotline' was created so US and Soviet leaders could communicate quickly in a future crisis.

questions.q: Who led the 1968 'Prague Spring' reforms in Czechoslovakia?
questions.explain: Dubcek's attempt to create 'socialism with a human face' was crushed by a Warsaw Pact invasion in 1968.

questions.q: The USSR formed the Warsaw Pact in 1955 mainly in response to which development?
options: West Germany being allowed to join NATO
The building of the Berlin Wall
The launch of the Marshall Plan
questions.explain: The rearming of West Germany within NATO prompted the USSR to bind its satellite states into the Warsaw Pact.

questions.q: A textbook argues that détente in the 1970s was collapsing by 1980. Which event best supports this claim?
options: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in 1979
The signing of SALT I in 1972
The building of the Berlin Wall
questions.explain: The 1979 invasion of Afghanistan shattered relations, prompting a US boycott of the 1980 Moscow Olympics.

questions.q: Which Soviet leader, in power from 1985, introduced the reforms of glasnost and perestroika?
questions.explain: Gorbachev's reforms of 'openness' (glasnost) and 'restructuring' (perestroika) helped bring the Cold War to an end.

questions.q: What did Gorbachev's policy of perestroika mean?
questions.explain: Perestroika meant 'restructuring', an attempt to reform and revive the failing Soviet economy.

questions.q: The Polish trade union Solidarity, led by Lech Walesa, was significant in the 1980s because it showed that:
options: Communist governments in Eastern Europe could be openly challenged
NATO was preparing to invade Poland
The USSR still controlled every satellite state firmly
the Warsaw Pact had already been dissolved
questions.explain: Solidarity's mass support demonstrated growing popular resistance to communist rule across the Eastern bloc.

questions.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall, symbolising the end of the Cold War division of Europe?
questions.explain: The Berlin Wall was opened in November 1989 as communist control across Eastern Europe collapsed.
